chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn 'Uthafir, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Condolences are not offered except at the grave. Then they should disperse, in case an event were to occur regarding the deceased, so they would hear the sound.

key_terms.التَّعْزِيَةُ: Condolences or comfort offered to the bereaved

ai.seo_question: Where should condolences be offered for the deceased according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the etiquette of ta'ziyah by specifying the grave as the primary venue for condolences, distinguishing it from the home visits common in other traditions. It further advises mourners to disperse promptly to avoid overhearing any post-mortem sounds from the body, reflecting a practical concern for the dignity of the deceased and the composure of the bereaved. This guidance underscores the Shia emphasis on brevity and propriety in mourning rituals, ensuring that the focus remains on the spiritual transition rather than prolonged physical observation.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Muhammad Bin Uzafar, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is no (offering of) condolences except by the grave. Then you should be dispersing, in case an event were to occur regarding the deceased, so you would be hearing the sound’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Isma’il from Muhammad ibn ‘Adhafir from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
condolence is offered only near the grave. Thereafter people should disperse so that if something should happen to the deceased no one can hear the voice.”
